Part I — July 29, 2026  ·  Part II — October

What This Is

Táukamí

The divine mark within all things.

On the Name

Tau  — τ — the 19th letter of the Greek alphabet. In numerology it reduces to 10, then to 1. Initiation. The self. New beginnings. The Tau cross appears in Egyptian Ankh tradition, in Pythagorean mystery schools, in Hermetic practice. In Hebrew, the letter Tav — the final letter of the alphabet — means mark or sign, signifying completion and covenant. In mathematics, tau (τ = 2π) represents the complete circle. Not half. The whole cycle.

Kami  — 神 — from the Shinto cosmological tradition of Japan — refers to the divine spirits inhabiting all living things. Not gods above us in a hierarchy. Presences within the world itself. Rivers, mountains, wind, the celestial bodies moving through the sky as you read this — all Kami. The divine is not separate from nature. It is nature, aware of itself.

Together — Táukamí — the divine mark within all things. The sacred signature woven through nature, time, and you.

What We Draw From

Hellenistic Astrology

Whole sign houses, planetary sect, bonification and maltreatment, the joys of the planets. Developed between 100 BCE and 700 CE, drawing on Babylonian and Egyptian sky-watching. Our primary ancient source: Vettius Valens. Our modern guide: Demetra George.

Sabian Symbols

Each of the 360 degrees of the zodiac holds its own image, its own instruction, its own medicine. Channeled by Elsie Wheeler in 1925, interpreted by Dane Rudhyar. The Sabian people of ancient Mesopotamia — the Moon Worshipers — are the ancestral thread behind this name.

Numerology

Pythagorean, Chaldean, and older forms. Pythagoras taught that number is the foundation of all things. This is not fortune-telling. It is pattern recognition at the level of mathematics and sound — two things that are ultimately the same.

Tarot

Rooted in 15th century Northern Italy, later synthesized with Kabbalistic and Hermetic tradition. An image language for the soul's movement through archetypal experience. Our interpretive foundation: Rachel Pollack's Seventy-Eight Degrees of Wisdom.

Herbalism

The oldest medicine on earth, practiced by every human culture. Grounds all practice in the body, in the earth, in the plant growing now in soil the moon is pulling water through. The Farmers' Almanac has tracked lunar planting calendars for over 200 years. Indigenous botanical knowledge predates that by millennia.

African Cosmological Frameworks

Particularly the philosophical traditions documented by Malidoma Patrice Somé — the understanding that nature speaks, that ancestors are present, that the visible and invisible worlds are not separate. This is not an addition to the practice. It is the root of it.

Hoodoo · Vodou

African diasporic spiritual practices forged in the crucible of the Americas — resilient, syncretic, and deeply practical. Hoodoo as folk magic rooted in African-American tradition. Vodou as a complete cosmological system carried from West Africa through Haiti and the diaspora. Both are ancestral inheritance, not aesthetic.

Astronomy · The Living Sky

Solar flares, geomagnetic storms, lunar cycles, weather patterns — the actual astronomical science mapped alongside astrological interpretation. Astrology is a reflection of what is happening in the cosmos, not its cause. The sky is not metaphor. It is fact, and it is speaking.

What to Bring

Curiosity Over Certainty

These systems are not meant to tell you what will happen. They are meant to help you see what is happening — in the sky, in your body, in the patterns of your life — with more clarity and more compassion.

Patience

The sky moves slowly. Saturn takes 29 years to complete one cycle around the sun. You are not going to understand your Saturn placement in one listening. That is the point. We are building a practice, not consuming content.

Presence

Every reading is recorded in real time — with the actual sky above us, with the actual planetary weather of this moment. This is not archived wisdom delivered from a distance. This is a living conversation between you, me, and the cosmos we are both moving through.

Waxing Crescent in Gemini

The New Moon in Taurus planted its seed on May 16. We are now two days into the waxing crescent — the phase of emergence, first movement, and early commitment to what was seeded in stillness. The Moon has moved into Gemini, quickening the energy with language, curiosity, and dual awareness.

The Farmers' Almanac names the waxing crescent as the time for planting above-ground crops, beginning new projects, and setting intention into motion. What seed did May 16 plant in you? This week asks it to speak its first word.
